d: A word which expresses blame, dislike, disapprobation, abhorrence, or contempt. See Fie.
A long bag net distended by hoops, into which fish can pass easily, without being able to return; -- called also fyke net. Cozzens.
A rebated cross, formerly used as a secret emblem, and a common ornament. It is also called gammadion, and swastika.
w.e: Prov. fr. AS. fy, fierf, feówerf. See Four, and Foot, n.

d: Fyrdung (, n. (Old. Eng. Hist.) “The military force of the whole nation, consisting of all men able to bear arms. The national fyrd or militia. J. R. Green.”
w.e: AS.; akin to E. fare, v. i.

d: 1. G is the seventh letter of the English alphabet, and a vocal consonant. It has two sounds; one simple, as in gave, go, gull; the other compound (like that of j), as in gem, gin, dingy. See Guide to Pronunciation, §§ 231-6, 155, 176, 178, 179, 196, 211, 246.
